correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the least possible embedding span as 1 plus cyclic-forward distances, proves endpoint deletion costs equal the endpoint distances, and proves every interior deletion reduces span by either zero or exactly one alphabet period. The two explicit inequalities are necessary and sufficient for all single deletions to be visible. The bijection of words with initial letter plus cyclic increments and finite-state transfer derives the all-alphabet formal series. The binary two-state reduction gives a rational bivariate series and Padovan recurrence. Exact-pole analysis proves the plastic-constant asymptotic. An independently implemented exhaustive word-level checker passed for 25 alphabet/window parameter pairs, with separate binary length-profile comparison. No finite test is asserted to prove unrestricted quantifiers.

value.rationale: The bounded-range subsequence model is meaningful in finite observation windows and difficult for general strings. For cyclic-permutation streams, the theorem completely classifies the minimal absent antichain for every alphabet size and window length and supplies a rational two-variable enumerator. The binary antichain has exponential growth at the plastic constant even though the observation trace has minimal period two; complete length layers are enumerated, not merely a routine membership test. This is a natural, parameter-uniform complete classification, and prior fixed-linear-word spectra do not determine the union-over-phases window antichain.
